payload.description:
When install finishes in a repository that already excludes the managed core from its linters, I want it to say nothing, so I can stop training a consumer to skim the region where a tracked CI edit is also reported.

Found by the terminal canary, filed there as term-ip2wz and pressed after it shipped twice unchanged. scaffolds.install_notes tests only whether a config file exists, never what it contains, so it advises extend-exclude on a .ruff.toml that has carried exactly that for releases. The canary verified the exclusion is genuinely in force rather than merely present: ruff format --check over the managed core exits 0 on 54 files.

The same block tells a consumer to hand-edit .pre-commit-config.yaml in a run that separately reports it has just rewritten that file.

Severity is low and nothing fails. The reason it is worth fixing is where it sits: the advice is the tail of the install output, and the tail is also where a re-pin of a tracked CI workflow is announced. Unactionable boilerplate beside a real edit teaches a reader to skip both.

Recorded against myself: this was already a requirement on basicly-fmgwtwi, which is still open, and I shipped two releases without meeting it while telling the canary it was on the record. It was on the record and it was not done.
payload.requirements: the check reads the file rather than testing its presence. A false skip is possible if the path is named for some other reason, and that is accepted and stated rather than guarded, because the cost of a missed note is one line a consumer can still read in the documentation.
payload.title: read the file before advising a change it already carries

payload.acceptance_criteria: external-facts says the control is built from a failure that has been seen rather than an assumed one, and says to check the denominator moved; the always-on surfaces stay under their caps and the projection gates pass
payload.description:
When an agent runs a positive control and it returns zero, I want the rule to say what the control must be built from, so I can stop reading a control's own zero as confirmation.

Asked for by the terminal canary as term-2vkce, and the request is well founded: the rule is in managed core they may never edit, they followed both halves of it, and still got a false reading. The wording said run a positive control and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. It never said what the control must be built from.

Their case is the evidence. They planted a table they called ragged; it was valid compact style, so it was never a violation, reported zero, and read exactly like a dead probe. Rebuilt from the defect actually observed - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - it reported two errors. What rescued the diagnosis was the denominator: 151 files became 152 when the control was added, which proved the file was read and sent them to the table rather than the tooling.

Three of my own false zeros the same day were the environment answering instead of the code. Theirs is the subtler one and the one the rule did not cover.

Carrying it in their overlay was the fallback, and the objection to that is right: two copies of one rule drift, and ours is the copy every other consumer reads.
payload.requirements: the amendment sits in the existing bullet rather than adding one, because the always-on budget is a standing cost on every consumer. The token cost declared on the fragment is updated to what the projection measures rather than left to drift.
payload.title: amend the positive control rule with what a control must be built from

payload.description:
When a patch release changes nothing the tutorial quotes, I want the page to need one edit rather than five, so I can stop paying a ten minute walkthrough for a version string.

Measured across v0.14.0, v0.14.1 and v0.14.2, all cut on 2026-09-18: each required the whole walkthrough re-run - install, scaffold, create, dor, classify, worktree, land, ship, log, status - and every quoted block matched apart from record ids, commit hashes and sub-second timings. Three runs, zero drift found, five strings edited each time.

The five sites are not one kind of thing and the gate cannot tell them apart. Line 7 is the claim, that every command and output was executed on a named version. Lines 36 and 50 are instructions, the uvx line a reader types. Lines 66 and 68 are transcript, what the tool printed.

The page already elides a timestamp on line 68 with its own convention, so eliding the version beside it is consistent rather than new.
payload.requirements: no quoted output is rewritten by a tool: the release may pin an instruction a reader types and may not touch a line the page presents as printed. The claim stays a human edit, because it is the sentence that must be true.
payload.title: stop a patch release costing a full tutorial re-record

payload.description:
A consumer upgrading a repository with basicly install cannot see which of their tracked files the run will touch until it has touched them. The run rewrites the vendored core catalog, the agent instruction files, the skills, the hooks, .gitattributes, .gitignore and the settings deny-list, and it keeps or overwrites a hand-edited core file depending on a recorded hash the consumer cannot read.

A dry run answers one question: which paths does this write, and which of my own edits does it keep. It writes nothing and exits 0.

payload.text:
[session handover 2026-09-19] Two releases cut and pushed; a fourth install-advice defect is fixed on main and deliberately unreleased.

STATE. main d0146315, clean, nothing unpushed. Tags v0.15.0 and v0.15.1 both pushed. Version on disk 0.15.1. uv run pytest -q -n 4 = 5909 passed 1 xfailed. uv run basicly verify --mode full = PASS.

SHIPPED IN v0.15.0. basicly install wires a post-merge hook that folds the writer shard a merge brought in and commits it with a record id the commit-msg gate accepts (basicly-z9s4iin). It resolves the engine at RUN time, not install time - a basicly on PATH, else the pinned uvx form - because the canary proved it has no basicly on PATH at all, so an install-time absolute path was a certain break rather than a risk. Both arms exercised under env -i. basicly install --dry-run (basicly-jgim0r0). The tutorial no longer costs a re-record per patch (basicly-8y8rxv4). basicly release refuses a stale tutorial transcript in preflight instead of writing everything and meeting the refusal at the commit gate (basicly-oror9os).

SHIPPED IN v0.15.1, both found by the canary within hours of the v0.15.0 tag. The managed-core exclusion advice was fixed into silence in v0.15.0: the check asked whether a config MENTIONS .basicly/core, never whether it EXCLUDES it, and this repo's own .ruff.toml names the path three times in per-file-ignores (basicly-ajqk150). install --dry-run reported the release's own headline feature as broken, because a dry run never syncs the catalog and so ran the vendored kit against the new engine's flags (basicly-v92kmjv); fixing that exposed a second fault under it, the kit computing its own script path even when a host supplies --command.

ON MAIN, UNRELEASED, OWNER'S CALL 2026-09-18. basicly-ap693b0: install advised adding exclude to the .pre-commit-config.yaml it writes itself, whose hooks lint .basicly/core on purpose - no-comments carries pass_filenames true and a files regex matching .py. Followed literally the advice disabled the gates the install had just written. Now silent until the config carries a hook basicly did not write. Held rather than cut because the canary was still on v0.15.0 and a third tag in one day is a version to skip. SHIPS IN THE NEXT CUT - do not let it sit.

OPEN, AND ONLY THE CANARY CAN CLOSE IT. Arm 1, the real fold: terminal-88 carries .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl at 30k, tracked, committed, never folded, hash d3afd42b recorded so the fold can be proven rather than assumed. It is armed but not exercisable - that side pushed, so it has nothing to pull; the fold fires the first time the other machine pushes and this one pulls. Every fold I have measured was on a shard I minted seconds earlier on a throwaway repo. This is the only real-ledger test there is.

ALSO OPEN. basicly-z79v2cf, a clock flake: test_supervise_board.py asserted 0 <= -1.439611 once inside verify --mode full, passed on re-run and 3 of 3 alone; it compares two clocks rather than one monotonic source. The tutorial claim line still forces a full walk on EVERY release including a patch, because docs-claims compares the transcript against the RELEASED version rather than the version it was recorded against - basicly-8y8rxv4 cut the pin cost, not this one, and it is unfiled. CI runs split across two SHAs on both releases: the tag's own commit ran the release job and a later tracker-only commit ran the other three, so 'green on the release commit' is not literally what exists.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING. Four defects this session were the same shape - a check that answers a question adjacent to the one asked. Mentions-vs-excludes, the dry run previewing an unsynced kit, a grep for a heading rather than for which file it names, a fixture whose directive was deleted while a comment still carried the path. Every one was caught by a row that MUST behave differently, never by the row that confirmed the hope.

Merged PR 2: PR 3 became CONFLICTING DIRTY (gh pr view 3 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus). Cause: the hook folds on a feature branch, so two PRs add the shared trunk file with different content.

s02-guarded-hook: hook folds only on the default branch. PRs 4-6; merged 4, b and c pulled main (no fold, shards kept), merged 5: PR 6 MERGEABLE CLEAN. s03-local-main-fold: dev1 and dev2 clones each pulled main (hook folded on local main, never pushed) at different shard sets and branched from it; merged PR 7: PR 8 CONFLICTING DIRTY. Conclusion: any automatic fold outside one serialized writer conflicts under a PR workflow. Readers read shards, so folding only bounds the file count. Decision (judgement call under the owner's never-conflict criterion): the fold hook is opt-in (--fold-on-merge; engine [tracker] fold_on_merge, default false, true in this repo where the engine is the single committer); compact runs as its own PR.
